A Turkish or European student at a school with no AP programme is not excluded from AP — they are excluded from the DEFAULT path, and the alternative has a hard November deadline. credential: UNO — "United Nations Online" (Stanley Prep / WFUNA)
tier: C — real programme, real NGO partner, but the UN attribution is overstated
LIVE_IN_ORYN: category=online_program, organization='Stanley Prep', cost=4000.00, verification_state='verified_current', cycle_status='open'. It is in our catalogue right now, marked verified and open, at $4,000.
partnership_IS_real: Confirmed bilaterally. WFUNA's own site: "Training Programs at the UN: Stanley Prep are developed by WFUNA and arranged through our educational partner, Stanley Prep", and it names the online product explicitly: "WFUNA's Online Training Program at the United Nations: Stanley Prep (UNO)."
what_WFUNA_actually_is: WFUNA's own about page: "The World Federation of United Nations Associations (WFUNA) is a global nonprofit organization representing and coordinating a membership of over 100 national United Nations Associations (UNAs) and their thousands of constituents." An independent NGO. NOT a UN organ and NOT a UN agency. Nothing on that page says WFUNA speaks for or represents the United Nations.
THE_DISCREPANCY: The two partners' own pages attribute the SAME credential to different issuers. WFUNA (which develops the programme and issues the credential) says: "Letter of Recommendation in Global Leadership from WFUNA" and "Official Certificate of Completion from WFUNA" — and states NOTHING about UN endorsement. Stanley Prep (the reseller) says: "Participants will receive an official recommendation letter from the United Nations", "Official certificate of completion and recommendation letter issued by the United Nations", and advertises a "UN-endorsed recommendation letter". A parent paying $4,000 reads the second version.
selection_gates_are_real: "The UNO program is highly selective, with only 50 participants chosen worldwide each year. Selection is based on academic excellence, leadership potential, and a demonstrated passion for international diplomacy." Concrete gates stated: "Rising 10th to 12th graders; Minimum high school GPA of 3.5" and "TOEFL 90 or above for non-US students".
cost: $4,000. Payment follows acceptance ("you will receive an email confirming your slot for the Spring 2026 cohort").
tier_recommendation: Do NOT assert a tier above open_enrollment yet. A stated GPA/TOEFL floor is a real eligibility gate, but a floor is not a selection RATE, and 'highly selective, only 50 chosen' is the vendor's own unverified claim. ingest.ts:190 requires the actual mechanism. `unknown` is the honest value pending WFUNA-side confirmation of how selection is run.
FOUNDER_DECISION: This is not fraud and should not be described as such — the programme, the partner and the gates are real. It is a $4,000 product whose marketing attributes to 'the United Nations' a credential its own developer attributes to an NGO. ORYN currently presents it as verified and open. Recommend: keep the row, correct the organization/description to name WFUNA as the developer, and never let the phrase 'from the United Nations' reach a student from our copy.

credential: UCAS Tariff points — how much an external certificate is actually worth in UK admissions
what_it_is: UCAS's own words: "UCAS Tariff points translate your qualifications and grades into a numerical value. Many qualifications (but not all) have a UCAS Tariff value, which will vary dependent on the qualification size, and the grade you achieved. This numerical value is used by HE course providers to assess whether you meet their entry requirements for a particular course."
THE_HONESTY_CAVEAT: Quoted COMPLETE, because the second half is the half that gets dropped: "Some universities, colleges, and conservatoires refer to UCAS Tariff points in their course entry requirements, but qualifications which do not receive Tariff points may be accepted too – so make sure you check the course entry requirements carefully." And: "Not all qualifications are on the Tariff, so don't worry if you can't find your qualification, as a university, college, or conservatoire may still accept it."
why_this_matters_for_ORYN: The Tariff is the single most-abused number in UK-facing admissions marketing. It is NOT universal — only SOME providers use it, and non-Tariff qualifications may be accepted anyway. ORYN must never render 'worth N UCAS points' as if it were an admissions outcome; that is precisely the false-precision the product spec forbids (non-negotiable #5). The honest framing is: some providers use this number, many do not, and the course page is the authority.
tariff_tables: UCAS publishes dated tables — '2026 Tariff tables' and '2027 Tariff tables' are both offered for download, so any stored Tariff figure must carry a cycle year.
music_grades_CLAIM_NOT_VERIFIED: A web-search summary gave specific point values for graded music exams (e.g. Grade 8 Performance Distinction = 30) offered by ABRSM/RSL/TCL/UWLQ. I did NOT verify these against the UCAS Tariff tables themselves — abrsm.org and the UCAS tables PDF both refused automated fetching. Recorded as UNVERIFIED. Do not publish these numbers without reading the official table.
access_note: WebFetch received 403 from ucas.com; the in-app browser reached the same page normally. Recording the 403 as a fact about our tool, not about UCAS.

credential: Digital consent age for Turkey (KVKK) vs UK/GDPR — resolves B4's 'not verified country-by-country' flag for ORYN's primary market
tier: A/B — multiple independent professional sources converge, but NOT directly quoted from KVKK's own regulatory text (PDF guides blocked, HTML pages don't state it inline)
finding: Checked kvkk.gov.tr directly (Turkey's official Personal Data Protection Authority) -- its general-principles HTML page does not state an age threshold inline, and its detailed children's-data guide is PDF-only (same structural wall hit 3x already tonight). Multiple INDEPENDENT Turkish law-firm/compliance analyses (CottGroup, Sengun Law, Kavlak Law Firm, Mondaq, Pandectes, all converging) state the same thing: unlike GDPR's explicit 13-16 member-state-chosen digital-consent age, Turkey's KVKK (Law No. 6698) sets NO specific minimum age for a minor's own data-processing consent at all. Instead, because Turkish civil law treats anyone under 18 as lacking full legal capacity, KVKK guidance places the burden on a PARENT/GUARDIAN to consent on any minor's behalf, full stop -- not just below a 13 or 16 threshold.
PRODUCT_IMPLICATION: This is MORE restrictive than the platform-stated 'age 13' bar (edX, Schoolhouse.world) or even GDPR's 16-in-some-countries bar that B4 already flagged as a trap. A Turkish 15-year-old is NOT below Coursera's stated 13 -- but under Turkish practice, parent/guardian involvement in the signup itself may still be the correct guidance for ORYN's core market regardless of which platform's number is quoted, because Turkish law doesn't recognize a minor's own consent as sufficient the way the platform's stated age implies. UK, by contrast, CONFIRMED at digital-consent age 13 -- matches platforms' own stated numbers exactly, no gap for UK users.
confidence_caveat: P2-strength sourcing: consistent across multiple independent professional legal sources, but not a direct quote from KVKK's own regulatory text or an official guide (both attempts blocked/inconclusive). Should be upgraded to P1 if someone can extract the PDF guide's actual text.

credential: DELF Junior cost -- genuinely has no single global price, same 'no single price to publish' shape already documented for Tufts/BU in Workstream A, just for a language exam instead of a program
min_age: N/A -- see the existing B9 entry for age (12-18, government-authorized). This is a follow-up on cost specifically.
cost_structural_finding: Unlike TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo (centralized, roughly uniform global administration), DELF/DALF is administered locally by each Alliance Francaise or approved test center, and EACH SETS ITS OWN FEE. A real official France-based table exists (godelf.com, presenting itself as official pricing): A1 EUR93, A2 EUR115, B1 EUR130, B2 EUR150. A separate US-specific table (a New York Alliance Francaise center) shows meaningfully different numbers for the SAME levels: A1 $135, A2 $145, B1 $155, B2 $190, plus a $5 administrative fee at that specific center. Neither figure is 'the' DELF Junior price -- both are real, both are for real test centers, and a Turkish student would see a third, different number from their own local Alliance Francaise. This is structurally the same shape as the 'price is a formula, not a number' pattern (Tufts/BU per-credit pricing) already documented in Workstream A's schema gaps -- not closable by picking one figure, only by recording the shape itself.
why_it_matters: If ORYN ever wants to show a DELF cost to a student, a single stored number would be wrong for the large majority of test centers by construction, not by research gap -- worth flagging this distinction (structural vs. simply-unresearched) the same way it was flagged for programs.
